title: Duke's lesson: why he never gave Jones a conductor's score
summary: Duke told Jones that a live show demanded knowing the score because there is no re-recording.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So did you ever get your conductor's score out of Duke?

I tell you what he did. He's never one lost for words, no matter what the situation is, you know, so he eventually made a reply, after I was walking around in shambles. He says, "Well, James, you know this is not like a recording date where you can go and re-record or patch over. You have to know the score, in case someone is missing. You will have to know what to do next or where to tell the band to go." And I couldn't argue with that point, you know. And he taught me that, but in such a way. He was a strange type of a teacher.
Yes, he was. I don't think there's anyone who's ever been associated with him that didn't learn a lot from him.
